canonical_statement: The study tests whether task-completion metrics can miss the interaction cost agents incur when they must reacquire execution-relevant state removed by context compression.
The primary controlled environment is IRBench, a deterministic project-planning task environment evaluated under a fixed 24-turn interaction horizon.
IRBench tool calls are decomposed into retrieval actions that reacquire external state and execution actions that perform task operations.
The protocol compares Full context, Sliding-window compression, a deterministic fact-preserving extractive Summary at matched budgets, and oracle state-restoration conditions.
Oracle restoration separates dropped state into externally queryable D-state and history-dependent R-state that is not recoverable from a single public query.

Primary comparisons use the same 10 seeds per condition and model, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, and Holm-Bonferroni correction across six retrieval comparisons; retention interventions use 20 paired seeds.
The study evaluates DeepSeek (deepseek-v4-flash), Qwen (qwen3.7-plus), and GPT-5.5 at temperature 0.3 without an explicit extended-thinking mode.
Retention interventions compact at turn 10 using digest budgets of 265, 100, or 50 tokens and compare multiple selection policies while holding digest format and placement fixed.

The D-Irrelevant follow-up holds digest format, position, budget, and retained R-state fixed while replacing D-state with fabricated out-of-universe content; it is reported as a post-hoc sequential diagnostic rather than a preregistered primary comparison.
The external-boundary probe uses 18 ALFWorld tasks across six task types with five paired seeds per task, yielding 90 paired cases and 180 runs.
Task completion is defined as the fraction of the ten required tasks completed within the fixed 24-turn horizon.

canonical_statement: The authors conclude that completion-only evaluation can miss substantial context-compression interaction cost because reacquisition behavior can increase before or without detectable completion loss.
For runtime design, the authors recommend focusing on which execution-relevant state would be costly to reacquire if dropped, rather than treating a compression ratio itself as universally safe.
The authors conclude that compression cost is conditional on the model, task regime, and environment recoverability rather than being an intrinsic consequence of shortening context.
The core mechanism was measured in two bounded, synthetic-adjacent environments, and specific cost magnitudes are not claimed to transfer to open-ended tasks.
Only three model families were evaluated; cross-model comparisons are descriptive and absolute cost counts are not fully comparable across serving providers.
The fixed 24-turn horizon is a design choice, and a different horizon could shift where interaction cost converts into task failure.
Tool-call count is a proxy for interaction cost rather than provider-dependent latency or dollar cost.
The retrieval-versus-execution decomposition is based on tool schema rather than semantic intention, and per-turn temporal call logs were not retained.
The extractive Summary is a designed fact-preserving control and does not establish that generic LLM-generated summaries are lossless.
Primary cells use 10 seeds, limiting statistical power for noisier completion outcomes despite paired analyses and reported confidence intervals.
The three-model comparison uses only the pre-specified 5× compression point; only DeepSeek receives a full severity sweep.
Only two main compression operators were evaluated, so results do not establish the cost patterns of abstractive summarizers or token-level compressors.
The D-Irrelevant control may conflate semantic irrelevance with verification of inconsistent or corrupt state content.
The selection null is established only on DeepSeek and the content intervention is replicated only on DeepSeek and GPT-5.5 at the loose budget, leaving model and budget generalization uncertain.

The acknowledgments state that AI language models assisted with portions of language translation and polishing, while experimental design, implementation, data collection, and analysis were conducted independently by the author.
